_about: Seed knowledge base of vertical-microdrama promo patterns, written for this assignment from the conventions of ReelShort / DramaBox-style ads. It is the RAG corpus for the picker: each episode retrieves the 3 most relevant patterns. Editors grow it: every promo they approve is appended to kb/approved_promos.jsonl and retrieved as a worked example for future shows.

patterns.name: Public humiliation
patterns.hook: Open mid-humiliation in front of a crowd: jilted at the altar, mocked at a party, slapped before guests.
patterns.cliffhanger: Cut as the victim's face hardens, or just before she answers back.
patterns.why: Instant injustice; the viewer sides with the underdog in under 3 seconds.
patterns.query: heroine publicly humiliated and mocked in front of a crowd of guests

patterns.name: Betrayal by family or lover
patterns.hook: Open on the cruelest line from the person who should protect her (fiance, sister, parent).
patterns.cliffhanger: End on her disbelieving question that nobody answers.
patterns.why: Betrayal by someone close is the genre's most reliable emotional trigger.
patterns.query: fiance or sister betrays her and the family takes their side

patterns.name: Disowned / stripped of status
patterns.hook: Open on the parent declaring 'you are no daughter of mine' or confiscating inheritance.
patterns.cliffhanger: Cut on her alone in the rain or on the villain's smirk.
patterns.why: Loss of status sets up the rags-to-riches payoff the audience wants to see.
patterns.query: father disowns her, revokes inheritance and casts her out

patterns.name: Physical cruelty
patterns.hook: Open on the strike itself: slap, whip, shove, hot iron raised. Sound of impact in the first second.
patterns.cliffhanger: Cut before the next blow lands or before rescue arrives.
patterns.why: A violent action is the strongest thumb-stopper; the open threat makes them stay.
patterns.query: villain strikes, whips, shoves or tortures the heroine

patterns.name: Cruel ultimatum
patterns.hook: Open on the villain naming an impossible price.
patterns.cliffhanger: Cut on 'do it, or he dies' and the heroine's silent decision.
patterns.why: An ultimatum is a built-in question: will she do it? The viewer must click to find out.
patterns.query: villain gives an ultimatum: do this humiliating thing or someone hangs

patterns.name: Mysterious protector steps in
patterns.hook: Open on the heroine cornered; a stranger's hand stops the attacker.
patterns.cliffhanger: Cut on the stranger's quiet threat or the villain asking 'who are you?'.
patterns.why: Protector fantasy plus a mystery about his identity.
patterns.query: mysterious scarred stranger intervenes and protects her from attackers

patterns.name: Unexpected proposal / contract marriage
patterns.hook: Open on a stranger kneeling with a ring in front of the people who rejected her.
patterns.cliffhanger: Cut before she answers, on the crowd's gasp.
patterns.why: The premise of the show in one image; it raises 'who is he?' and 'will she say yes?'.
patterns.query: stranger kneels and proposes marriage to the rejected bride in front of everyone

patterns.name: Hidden identity hint
patterns.hook: Open on an object that should not belong to a poor man: a crest, a signet ring, a uniform.
patterns.cliffhanger: Cut as someone asks 'who gave you this?' or 'what is your husband's name?'.
patterns.why: Dramatic irony: viewers know the title promise ('he was a Duke') and want the reveal.
patterns.query: a ring or crest hints that the poor husband is secretly a nobleman

patterns.name: Identity reveal
patterns.hook: Open on the villain's face as the hero walks in, transformed, through smoke or doors.
patterns.cliffhanger: Cut on the villain's 'it can't be you' before the hero answers.
patterns.why: The payoff fantasy. High spoiler risk, so use only when the title already promises it.
patterns.query: the husband walks in revealed as the true duke and the villains are shocked

patterns.name: Framed and arrested
patterns.hook: Open on the accusation or handcuffs: 'you are under arrest'.
patterns.cliffhanger: Cut on 'take her away' as she is dragged off protesting.
patterns.why: Injustice plus danger; the viewer wants to see the truth come out.
patterns.query: heroine falsely accused, framed and dragged away by guards

patterns.name: Underdog clapback
patterns.hook: Open on the villain's insult, then the heroine's sharp reply in under 10 seconds.
patterns.cliffhanger: Cut on the villain's furious reaction and a threat.
patterns.why: Satisfying defiance is shareable; the threat leaves the score unsettled.
patterns.query: heroine answers the villain's insult with a defiant comeback

patterns.name: Sacrifice for love
patterns.hook: Open on the heroine walking into pain for him (thorns, fire, prison).
patterns.cliffhanger: Cut while she is still suffering and he is screaming her name.
patterns.why: Devotion under torment pairs romance with suspense.
patterns.query: she endures pain and injury to save her husband while he begs her to stop

patterns.name: Rescue from danger
patterns.hook: Open on the danger: fire, attack, a blade at her throat.
patterns.cliffhanger: Cut before we know if they both make it out.
patterns.why: Life-or-death stakes with a protector arc.
patterns.query: house on fire or attack at night, he rushes in to save her

patterns.name: Villain plotting
patterns.hook: Open on the villain's whispered plan or poison vial.
patterns.cliffhanger: Cut on the villain's smile as the trap is set.
patterns.why: Dramatic irony: the viewer knows the danger the heroine does not. Weaker standalone.
patterns.query: villains secretly plot, poison or scheme against the heroine

patterns.name: Interrupted ceremony
patterns.hook: Open on vows or a wedding at its peak.
patterns.cliffhanger: Cut as the doors burst open or someone shouts 'stop this wedding'.
patterns.why: A guaranteed open loop: who is at the door?
patterns.query: wedding ceremony interrupted as the doors burst open

patterns.name: Quiet tenderness (weak ad)
patterns.hook: Gentle bonding moment by the fire, bandaging wounds, a soft confession.
patterns.cliffhanger: Usually resolves; rarely an open loop.
patterns.why: Good for retention inside the app, weak as a cold-audience ad. Use only with a hard cut to danger.
patterns.query: tender quiet moment between husband and wife by the fire
